title: Keeping characters consistent in an AI-assisted RPG opening
author: teamJayK
selftext:
I drew the cast and storyboarded the opening for my tactical RPG, Year without a Summer. I made the animation with Claude and Seedance. Seedance generated the shots, and I spent days retouching frames by hand to keep the characters recognizable. For the latest cut, I rebuilt some shots from scratch.



[Full opening on YouTube](https://youtu.be/P29_--a2luk)

replies.author: Tarkov_Apologist
replies.body: For 3d use a model template, write a core description of the style and what you want it to produce. For sprites Ive started working with rigs and turning them into sprite sheets. Very helpful for composite stuff, but it's also not bad for one off animations.

replies.author: teamJayK
replies.body: Thanks! I’m still learning myself, so I don’t have a definitive answer. In my experience, making multiple attempts, using high-resolution character sheets, and bringing Claude into the workflow all seemed to improve my chances of getting consistent results.

comments.author: teamJayK
comments.body: Thanks! For the early version, I went frame by frame on the shots that needed it. These days I mostly throw money at the problem and pay for a few more generations 😄
